title: Alter Ego
build: Male edition, the C64 Preservation Project original disks (alter_ego_male_s1 to s6, Activision 1987)

records.c: The life program's load address and entry: JMP gameplay_object_entry_setjmp ($B392). call_vm_function_pointer in the resident program calls whatever object is at $8466 this way; the start object's entry is at the same address.

The six zero-terminated lines of the RUN/STOP menu, which the descriptor at $CAB1 points at: "    Do you wish to:", "     CONTINUE", "     SAVE GAME", "     RESUME GAME", "     QUIT" and "     DISPLAY STATUS, THEN ASK ME AGAIN". The spaces before each line indent it in the panel.

The life program's main procedure: one phase of life after another. It reads the stage's header (load_stage_header), works out how many ages the map has ($CAD5, a third of $82BB) and the last age with a cell still in it ($CAD3, the age at the window's foot), counts the cells left ($CAD7), sets the border to the stage's colour ($CAA4 + stage - 1) and, on a new stage, plays its first cell at once (on stage 1, after drawing five rows from the cell words at $C29C and waiting for fire). Then the map window is drawn and the arrow (sprite 0) put on it, and every key moves it: up and down a row (scrolling the window at its edges), left and right over the three cells and the two choice columns beside them. Fire plays the cell under the arrow, or the choice beside the map; f1-f8 a choice by number. RUN/STOP opens the menu at $CAB1: continue, save, resume, quit (the longjmp out with 1) or the status pages.
Inputs: +8 the entry's pointer; +10 0 for a new stage, 1 to read the header over a saved or resumed game.
Outputs: none; it leaves only through gameplay_object_longjmp_exit.

Open the stage's file, unless $CADB says it is open: MAP2 for stage 7, MAP<n> for the others, through the open at $5B72. While the open fails it asks for the disk again (prompt_retry_after_disk_error) and redraws the map after, when +8 is set. $CADB is then the stage's number. On stages 1, 2 and 7 the file starts with a four-byte offset, which it reads into a local and, except on stage 2, seeks to.
Inputs: +8 1 to redraw the map after a retry.
Outputs: 0, or $CADB when it was open.

Read the stage's header from its file: eight bytes of its clock ($803B-$8042, the first age at $803B), the 48 bytes of its choices ($81C5), the count of its map words ($82BB) and the map, three words an age ($81F7), the cell the arrow starts on ($82DB), the count of its scene blocks ($82F5) and each block's length ($82FB); then the file's position, where the blocks start, goes to $82F7 (the tell at $5EAD). A negative stage number at $82BD means a stage just begun: it is made positive and the header read in full. When +8 is set (a game resumed or saved) the choices, the map and the start cell are read into a 514-byte local instead, and the ones in memory kept. The age ($7F74) is brought up to the stage's first. A short read reports one of the texts at $89DC and closes the file.
Inputs: +8 keep.
Outputs: +8, or -1 when the file was short.

Play the scene block behind a map cell or a choice. The 64 shared words ($7F40) are copied to $8145 first, so that a scene that is not to count can put them back. A choice's block comes from run_stage_choice_experience; a cell's word gives its block, found with locate_scene_block, and execute_scene_chunk_chain plays its scenes. Their value says what follows: another of the choice's experiences, the profile panel (the texts at $8CA5 when there is nothing for the player), the cell crossed off, or the stage over. The block's length (a third of it for a choice) moves the years and the money on (advance_age_and_finances). The stage ends when the age passes its last or no cell is left, and finish_life_stage runs.
Inputs: +8 column (or choice / 4); +10 row (or choice & 3); +12 the age at the window's foot, or -1; +14 1 for a choice.
Outputs: 1 when the stage ended, else 0.

The three lines play_life_map_cell shows in the profile panel when a block's scenes held for nobody: "I'm sorry, this experience is", "inappropriate for you at this" and "time. Please try again later."

The end of a stage. The text panel is wiped, the stage's file closed, and the RUN/STOP menu ($CAB1) shown until its answer is not the status. Then on to the next stage: after the seventh, the first again, with the 88 bytes from $7F58 cleared, the acquisitions ($82AB) gone and the bytes 00 00 70 2A at $7FC0; otherwise the debt is paid in part, its share for the stages left (debt thousands $7F84 / $8041) taken from the cash thousands ($7F78), or all the cash when the share is more, and the debt's units ($7F82) cleared. The new stage number is stored negative, so that its header is read in full. Then the menu's answer: continue, save (save_current_game_menu), resume (resume_saved_game_menu) or quit (the longjmp out with 1).
Inputs: none.
Outputs: the menu's answer, or what the save or resume returned.

Play choice +9's next experience. The choice's word at $81C5 gives the first of its scene blocks (its low byte + 1) and its type; the 32 bits at $81D5 + 4 x choice say which of them are left (for a type-6 choice, less the bits at $7FC0, those had already). It walks the bits from the lowest: for each one set it finds the block (locate_scene_block) and plays it (execute_scene_chunk_chain). A value of -3 (no alternative held) goes on to the next bit; any other stores the block's length at +11, crosses the bit off (a type-6 choice adds it to $7FC0) and returns the value. With none left, +13 set returns -3; clear, the panel says there is nothing more for now (texts at $9122) or ever (at $9179, when the mask is empty), +11 gets 0 and the value is $FE. The bit is doubled with the 32-bit multiply at $6E9F.
Inputs: +9 the choice; +11 where to put the length; +13 flag.
Outputs: the scene chain's value, $FE or -3 ($FFFD).

Two sets of three lines for run_stage_choice_experience when a choice has no experience to give: "None of these experiences is", "appropriate for you at this", "time. Please try again later." ($9122) while some are left but none held, and "There are no more experiences", "for this icon in this module.", "Please try again later." ($9179) when they are all used.

Move the years and the money on by a scene block of length +9. The length times the stage's years per unit ($803F), in 1024ths of a year, goes onto the year's fraction ($7FC4); the whole years carried go onto the age ($7F74) and $7F8C. Cash ($7F78 thousands and $7F76 units) and debt ($7F84, $7F82) are worked in whole units with the 32-bit helpers at $6E9F-$6F1D, and cash below nothing goes onto the debt. With a salary ($7F8A, while $7F58 is set) the years' pay is added less a tax worked from $7F52 and the stages left ($8041); without one, the stages up to the sixth (5 >= $8041) cost a fifth of the years' worth of cash. At the end an acquisition waiting at $7F88 becomes its bit at $82AB (1 shifted left by it, $B50C) and $7F88 is cleared.
Inputs: +9 the block's length.
Outputs: none.
The $7059 header's first byte: advance_age_and_finances keeps 0 bytes of the workspace from $30 in its frame, which the epilogue at $70D1 puts back.

advance_age_and_finances: the years' earnings. With no job ($7F58 zero) the salary $7F8A is cleared. A salary adds its pay for the years, less a tax worked from $7F52 and the stages left ($8041); without one the branch at $9629 takes the cost of living on the stages up to the sixth.

advance_age_and_finances: the cash and the debt, worked as 32-bit units in the frame, divided by 1000 back into thousands and units ($7F78/$7F76, $7F84/$7F82); then an acquisition waiting at $7F88 becomes its bit at $82AB.

Read the header of the scene block that locate_scene_block found. It opens the stage's file (open_stage_map_stream, with redraw), seeks to the block's place ($CC65), reads its unpacked and packed lengths ($CADF, $CAE1) and the count of its scenes ($CAE3), then their boundaries ($CAE5, a word each), and notes where its packed bytes start ($CAAB). Nothing is unpacked: $CAAF and $CAD1 are set to 0 and the decoder reset ($A4E1). On a failure it reports one of the texts at $99BC; from $998B it looks at the file status ($8043 & 15): a missing or broken file (6, 7 or 15) reports "Fatal Disk Error!" and leaves through gameplay_object_longjmp_exit with -1; any other closes the file and tries again from the start.
